key_concepts: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.
Isotopes have different mass numbers but the same number of protons.
Isotopes of an element have the same chemical properties.
Carbon-12, carbon-13, and carbon-14 are isotopes of carbon.
Average atomic mass is calculated from the relative abundances of isotopes.
Cesium, thorium, and zirconium average atomic masses can be computed from isotope abundanc
The periodic table atomic mass of neon (20.180 amu) is a weighted average of its isotopes.
Nitrogen-14, nitrogen-15, and nitrogen-16 differ in neutron number and have different uses
Isotopes have real-world applications such as carbon dating, medical imaging, and nuclear
Oxygen isotopes O-16, O-17, and O-18 are used in climate science to reconstruct past clima
